title: Majorana parity qubit in coupled minimal Kitaev chains
authors: Francesco Zatelli, Bart Roovers, Nick van Loo, Antonio Lombardi, Juan D. Torres Luna, Sebastian Miles, Vincent P. M. Sietses, Florian J. Bennebroek Evertsz', Pablo Cova Fariña, Alberto Bordin, Ghada Badawy, Erik P. A. M. Bakkers, Michael Wimmer, Leo P. Kouwenhoven
abstract: Majorana zero modes provide a route to fault-tolerant qubits by encoding information non-locally in fermion parity. Their sensitivity to noise is expected to decrease exponentially with increasing separation between the Majoranas, a suppression known as topological protection. Kitaev chains engineered in quantum dot-superconductor arrays provide a tunable platform in which separated Majorana zero modes can emerge at the ends of the chain, even in two-site chains. These minimal-chain modes are known as poor man's Majoranas and retain characteristic Majorana properties, including near-zero energy and equal electron-hole character, but have only limited protection. A key outstanding challenge is to move beyond identifying such modes in electrical transport measurements and achieve coherent qubit control in the time domain. Here, we demonstrate a Majorana parity qubit by realizing coherent coupling between two-site Kitaev chains. Since total fermion parity is conserved, the system separates into global even and odd parity manifolds. We observe coherent parity oscillations in both manifolds with equal oscillation frequencies at the Majorana sweet spot, as predicted for isolated Majorana zero modes. We further show that the oscillation frequency and coherence depend systematically on inter-chain coupling and quantum-dot detunings, in close agreement with our model for short, partially protected chains. Our results establish the first coherent control of a Majorana qubit, encoded in the fermion parity of Majorana zero modes in minimal Kitaev chains.
summary: The research demonstrates the first coherent control of a Majorana qubit by engineering two coupled minimal Kitaev chains in superconducting nanowires. By observing Rabi oscillations between global even and odd parity states, the authors confirm that the system can be manipulated coherently using electrical pulsing techniques. This work advances the field by moving topological qubits from theoretical identification to measurable quantum computation.
main_problem: The primary goal is to move beyond merely identifying Majorana zero modes via transport measurements and achieve genuine, coherent qubit control using these modes encoded in fermion parity.
main_result: The authors demonstrated the first instance of coherent control over a Majorana qubit by observing measurable, Rabi-like parity oscillations in both the even and odd global parity manifolds.
method: Coherent dynamics were measured using pulsed charge-stability measurements, monitoring the shift in a radio-frequency resonator's resonance frequency due to parity-dependent quantum capacitance.
model_or_system: The system is realized using two coupled minimal Kitaev chains engineered in quantum dot–superconductor arrays. The physics is modeled by separating the Hamiltonian into global even and odd parity manifolds based on fermion parity conservation.
key_observables: Coherent parity oscillations (Rabi oscillations) in both even and odd manifolds, and the systematic dependence of oscillation frequency/coherence on inter-chain coupling and detunings.
important_parameters: Inter-chain coupling ($\epsilon_{23}$), quantum-dot detunings ($\epsilon_{12}, \epsilon_{34}$), superconducting phase ($\phi$), and magnetic field ($B_\perp$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the effective Hamiltonian derived for the even/odd manifolds, and some later analyses assume first-order dependence on detuning near the sweet spot.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the device schematic (Fig. 1a), Bloch sphere rotations (Fig. 1b), energy spectra showing state splitting (Fig. 1c), and pulsed charge-stability diagrams mapping parity transitions ($p(oo|oo)$) as a function of gate voltages.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing the theoretical framework for the Majorana parity qubit in coupled chains, to demonstrating coherent control via parity oscillations, and finally analyzing the dependence of these dynamics on various tunable parameters like coupling strength and detuning.
why_interesting: This work provides direct experimental evidence of controlled quantum evolution (Rabi oscillations) using topological qubits, which is a major milestone for solid-state quantum computing architectures.
